newsitem.title: USA: J.P. Morgan shares off ahead of Q2 earnings.
newsitem.headline: J.P. Morgan shares off ahead of Q2 earnings.

text.p: J.P. Morgan & Co Inc's shares were lower early Wednesday afternoon amid uneasiness about the banking and financial services company's second-quarter earnings, due out Thursday, traders and analysts said.

In early June, Robert Albertson at Goldman, Sachs & Co was among the analysts that lowered second-quarter estimates on J.P. Morgan earnings. They said fixed-income proprietary trading was soft early in the quarter.
Albertson said Wednesday it was unclear whether the business turned around in June.

Analysts on average have estimated J.P. Morgan would earn $1.75 a share, according to a First Call survey. That compares with earnings of $2.04 in the first quarter of 1997 and $2.14 in the second quarter of 1996.
J.P. Morgan shares were down 2-1/2 at 107 in afternoon trading.

Traders and analysts said the announcement by Wells Fargo and Co that its second-quarter earnings would fall short of estimates had no bearing on J.P. Morgan's situation. Earlier, Wells Fargo said unexpected expenses related to its $11 billion acquisition of First Interstate would hold back its earnings, due out next week.
"I think it's (Wells Fargo) very much company-specific," said one trader, noting that some bank stocks were down with the overall market.
"Wells is a totally separate issue" from J.P. Morgan," Albertson said.
